newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: FOCUS-Tariff hike to boost Tenaga profits.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Tariff hike to boost Tenaga profits.

text.p: Malaysia's announcement of an 8.3 percent hike in electricity tariff for Tenaga Nasional Bhd on Wednesday would add 300-400 million ringgit ($120-160 million) to the utility's bottomline in 1998, analysts said.

"... The government has agreed to allow Tenaga Nasional Bhd to raise electricity tariffs by 1.8 cents per unit, that is from 21.7 cents an average unit now to 23.5 cents an average unit from May 1, 1997," Energy, Telecommunications and Posts minister Leo Moggie announced at a news conference.

"The rate hike should contribute around 300 million ringgit to (Tenaga's) earnings, and it should be fully reflected in the 1998 earnings," said Soh Meng Hui, head of research at K.L. City Securities.
"A one cent increase would translate to an additional 400 million ringgit to the bottomline," said Amarjit Chhina, analyst with BZW in Malaysia.
Most analysts said the hike was within expectations.
"We were expecting around an eight percent (tariff hike), so the 8.3 percent hike was slightly better than expected," said Sharinaz Shafie, power analyst at ABN Amro Hoare Govett in Kuala Lumpur.
Tenaga had been lobbying for almost one year for the rate hike, and analysts said their recommendations were pegged on whether Tenaga would receive one in 1997, and on the amount of the increase.
Moggie said the tariff increase was unavoidable as generating costs had increased and were beyond Tenaga's control.

The presence of Independent Power Producers like YTL Corporation Bhd had impacted Tenaga's potential earnings growth, as Tenaga is obliged to buy power from them, analysts said. A tariff hike was thus seen as crucial for the conmpany's earnings growth.
"We had a 'sell' on the stock at 12.90 ringgit, but we are upgrading it to a 'hold' now because any news like this will be better for the market and especially for Tenaga," said Sharinaz.
Others were even more bullish on the news.

"With the tariff hike it should be a buy, because now it will translate into a more solid earnings growth. The share price had dropped sharply in one week, so at this price it's a buy," said Soh Meng Hui at K.L. City Securities.
At the close of the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange, Tenaga was 70 cents higher at 11.60 ringgit.

Moggie said that Tenaga may not get another rate hike in the next few years. He said this was possible due to the fixing of gas prices for Tenaga at 6.40 ringgit/mmBtu (million British thermal units) up to the year 2000 against 7.0 ringgit now.
The minister added that the government had "initiated a study for a future long-term tariff plan" to be conducted over the next few years.
